items.name: HIIT 2x/week
items.notes: Structured interval training twice weekly, assumed to replace easier cardio. Modeled as a somewhat larger CRF stimulus with diminishing marginal return.

items.name: HIIT 3x/week
items.notes: Three structured interval sessions weekly, assumed to replace easier cardio. Modeled with extra recovery uncertainty and a small recurring downside because current frequency evidence suggests no clear added benefit over 2x/week in recreational runners.

items.name: Tempo run 1x/week
items.notes: One threshold/tempo-style run weekly, assumed to replace easier cardio. Modeled as intermediate between easy cardio and HIIT for CRF benefit.

items.name: HIIT 1x/week
items.notes: Structured interval training once weekly, assumed to replace an easier cardio session rather than add volume. Modeled through modest CRF/VO2max utility, not a direct mortality claim.

items.name: Zone 2 cardio 2x/week
items.notes: Two structured low-to-moderate intensity cardio sessions weekly, assumed to replace unstructured easier running. Modeled as a small CRF and recovery-positive intervention.

items.name: Strength maintenance
items.notes: Structured resistance training intended to preserve strength. Modeled conservatively because its marginal value depends heavily on the training already in your routine.

items.name: Metformin
items.notes: Bannister 2014: diabetics on metformin outlived controls. TAME pending.

items.name: Statin
items.notes: CTT meta: 21% CVD reduction per mmol/L LDL.

access.notes: Over-the-counter nasal steroid. Easy to trial without specialist access.

items.name: Nasacort nightly
items.notes: Best-supported for congestion-mediated sleep disturbance and as an adjunct in nasal-obstruction OSA phenotypes. Main benefit is upper-airway, not general prevention.

access.notes: Usually requires a prescription plus a DME supplier, but often has better coverage than branded insomnia drugs.

items.name: APAP nightly
items.notes: Modeled as the strongest pre-diagnosis airway intervention candidate. No direct mortality term; benefit comes through sleep-burden and sleep-mortality relief.

items.name: GLP-1 RA
items.notes: SELECT trial: HR 0.80 MACE in overweight/obesity with established CVD. Strong transport shrinkage applied for lean, low-risk profiles plus GI/gallbladder harms.

access.notes: Usually needs a dentist or sleep specialist plus custom fabrication. Coverage is more variable than PAP.

items.name: Custom oral appliance
items.notes: Custom mandibular advancement device, annualized over replacement and follow-up. Typically less effective than PAP but often easier to tolerate.

access.notes: Over-the-counter and easy to test immediately, but usually only a modest airway aid.

items.name: Nasal strips nightly
items.notes: Primarily a subjective nasal-congestion and snoring aid. Helps when the problem is upper-airway narrowing, but usually not a large standalone OSA treatment.

access.notes: Low-friction bedroom hardware, but only attractive if the room is actually dry and you keep humidity in a safe range.

items.name: Humidifier nightly
items.notes: Modeled as a small dryness / nasal-comfort intervention, not a meaningful standalone OSA treatment. Best case is low ambient humidity or waking with dry irritated nasal passages.
